metadata.note: Only entries with documented sources are included.

immediate_actions: Remove and discard visibly infected leaves and plant parts.
Remove fallen infected plant debris around the plant.
Avoid wetting foliage during irrigation.
cultural_control: Improve air circulation around the plant.
Keep foliage as dry as practical.
chemical_control: Use a fungicide only when the product is registered/labeled for the crop and disease.
Follow the local product label for dose, interval, protective equipment and harvest/re-entry restrictions.
prevention: Inspect plants regularly for new leaf spots.
safety_notes: Do not recommend a pesticide solely from this diagnosis.
Product registration and permitted crops vary by country and location.

immediate_actions: Remove infected leaves and infected canes where practical.
Collect and remove fallen infected leaves.
Water at the soil rather than wetting the foliage.
chemical_control: A labeled fungicide may be used to protect new foliage when appropriate.
Follow the local product label exactly.
safety_notes: Pesticide products must be registered/labeled for the intended crop and disease.
Follow all label and personal-protection requirements.

immediate_actions: Remove severely infected leaves or shoots where practical.
Improve air circulation around the plant.
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization unless a soil test indicates a need.
cultural_control: Prune appropriately to improve light penetration and airflow.
Avoid practices that encourage excessive lush new growth.
chemical_control: Fungicides can protect healthy tissue when applied early.
Possible active ingredients include sulfur or potassium bicarbonate where legally labeled for the crop and disease.
Follow the product label for application interval and safety requirements.
prevention: Begin appropriate protection when symptoms first appear rather than waiting for severe infection.
safety_notes: Fungicides generally protect healthy tissue rather than curing established infection.
Always follow the pesticide label and verify that the product is permitted for the crop.
recommendations.source_title: Powdery mildew on trees and shrubs

immediate_actions: Remove infected flowers, leaves and stems.
Dispose of infected plant material appropriately.
Avoid overhead watering.
cultural_control: Improve air circulation by appropriate spacing.
Keep foliage and flowers as dry as practical.
Avoid wounding plants during handling and pruning.
chemical_control: For garden flowers, cultural control is often sufficient.
If a fungicide is considered, use only a product labeled for the specific crop and disease.
prevention: Reduce prolonged wetness and high humidity around foliage.
Remove old or wounded plant tissue promptly.
safety_notes: Follow local pesticide labels and safety requirements.
Do not apply an agricultural chemical solely because the model predicts gray mold.
recommendations.source_title: Gray mold in the flower garden

immediate_actions: Remove and discard severely infected leaves or plants.
Avoid overhead irrigation and leaf wetting.
Disinfect tools after working with infected plants.
cultural_control: Avoid splashing water from soil or debris onto foliage.
chemical_control: Do not automatically prescribe an antibiotic or bactericide.
Use only a product specifically registered and labeled for the crop and bacterial disease in the farmer's location.
prevention: Maintain sanitation of tools, benches and growing areas.
safety_notes: Bacterial leaf symptoms can resemble other leaf-spot diseases.
Confirm the diagnosis before chemical treatment.

immediate_actions: Remove severely infected plant material.
Avoid overhead irrigation.
Clean and disinfect tools and containers.
cultural_control: Separate handling of infected debris from healthy plants.
chemical_control: Use a bactericide only if it is specifically labeled for the diagnosed crop and disease.
prevention: Avoid moving contaminated soil or debris onto healthy foliage.
safety_notes: Several bacterial pathogens can cause visually similar spots, blights and wilts.

immediate_actions: Remove and destroy affected leaves and disease debris.
Avoid excessive irrigation and prolonged leaf wetness.
cultural_control: Avoid practices that splash water from infected debris onto foliage.
chemical_control: If chemical control is required, use only a fungicide labeled for chrysanthemum and Septoria/leaf spot in the local jurisdiction.
prevention: Monitor plants during cool and wet periods.
safety_notes: Chemical treatment should follow local registration and label requirements.

immediate_actions: Remove and discard rotting plant tissue.
Separate severely affected plants from healthy plants where practical.
Reduce excess moisture around the plant.
cultural_control: Avoid injuries to stems and roots.
Maintain clean growing areas and equipment.
chemical_control: Do not automatically recommend a pesticide.
Treatment depends on the organism causing the rot and should be confirmed before chemical use.
safety_notes: Soft rot symptoms can have different causes, including bacterial and fungal organisms.
Diagnosis should be confirmed before selecting a chemical treatment.

immediate_actions: Remove and destroy severely wilted infected plants.
Inspect nearby plants for similar symptoms.
Use disease-free planting material.
biological_control: TNAU reports use of Pseudomonas fluorescens with rooted chrysanthemum cuttings as part of wilt management.
chemical_control: Do not automatically recommend a fungicide solely from the image diagnosis.
Confirm the causal organism and follow the locally registered product label.
prevention: Avoid carrying infected plant material between growing areas.
safety_notes: Wilt can have fungal, bacterial or physiological causes.

immediate_actions: Check irrigation, drainage and recent environmental stress.
Inspect leaves for the pattern of yellowing.
Consider soil or leaf testing before applying nutrients.
cultural_control: Correct documented nutrient or soil-pH problems rather than applying nutrients blindly.
prevention: Use soil or plant testing when nutrient deficiency is suspected.
safety_notes: Chlorosis is a symptom, not necessarily a single disease.
The model should not automatically prescribe iron or another nutrient without evidence of deficiency.

immediate_actions: Remove severely affected leaves, flowers or stems where practical.
Remove diseased debris from around plants.
Avoid prolonged leaf wetness.
chemical_control: Use a fungicide or bactericide only after confirming the likely cause and checking the local product label.
safety_notes: Blight is a broad symptom category and can be caused by different pathogens.

immediate_actions: Check soil moisture and irrigation.
Check for recent heat, strong sunlight or hot dry wind.
Inspect affected leaves for signs of pests or disease.
cultural_control: Maintain adequate root-zone moisture without overwatering.
Reduce exposure to extreme heat where practical.
prevention: Monitor plants during periods of high temperature and dry wind.
Maintain appropriate irrigation and growing conditions.
safety_notes: Leaf scorch can be caused by environmental stress and is not automatically an infectious disease.
Do not recommend pesticides solely from a scorch prediction.
recommendations.source_title: Keep gardens thriving through the heat
